title: A Sigil for the Crown
premise: Juniper Whitlock's debts to the Thornfell temple bind him to a life of careful invisibility, copying prayers by day and guiding smugglers by night. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, he learns the court beneath the mountain has bought his sister Wren's soul as payment for an old family bargain struck before his birth. Guided by a disgraced ward-keeper and hunted by the temple's enforcers who want him silenced, Juniper must cross the darkened mountains and outwit the Undercourt before the thirteenth moonrise seals the sale forever. He succeeds only by offering the one thing more valuable than a soul: his own name and inheritance, dissolving himself into the mountain's memory so Wren can walk free into a world where stars are learning to burn again.
about_author: Sebastian Montrose is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about debt, borders, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: Ink and Indenture
chapters.summary: Juniper copies temple ledgers under a master who counts every candle he burns, establishing the crushing weight of his inherited debt. At night he guides a smuggler caravan through Thornfell passes. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: weary competence masking a longing for a life that isn't borrowed.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Juniper discovers a sealed page in the temple archives bearing his family name and a transaction mark from thirteen years ago. His questions earn him a beating from the head scribe. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: first crack in his carefully maintained invisibility.

chapters.title: Wren at the Well
chapters.summary: Juniper visits his sister Wren in the lowland village, where she seems strangely pale and forgets words mid-sentence. A traveling star-reader warns that the sky is 'thinning.' POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: dread blooming beneath ordinary affection.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: The border wards shatter like glass and every star above Thornfell goes dark simultaneously. Smugglers scatter; the temple locks its gates. Juniper finds the ward-keeper Halvard half-dead in the pass. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: terror and a terrible sense of recognition.

chapters.title: What Halvard Remembers
chapters.summary: Halvard reveals the wards were fed by souls sold to the Undercourt, and that the Whitlock bargain purchased Wren's protection—until now. The temple wants both siblings erased as evidence. POV: alternating Juniper/Halvard. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged in shared guilt.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: Halvard explains the terms: the soul-sale completes on the thirteenth new moon unless reclaimed by blood kin at the Undercourt's threshold. They have twelve turns. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: hope arriving wrapped in a deadline.

chapters.title: The Temple's Hounds
chapters.summary: Enforcer-scribes led by Brother Cassian hunt Juniper through the foothills, burning villages that sheltered him. Juniper uses smuggler roads to stay ahead. POV: Cassian interlude shows his zealous certainty. Emotional beat: being seen is now lethal.

chapters.title: The Salt Road
chapters.summary: A desperate crossing of the salt flats where the darkened sky makes navigation impossible; Juniper navigates by memory alone, proving his worth to Halvard. They rescue a stranded child, Maren, who insists on following. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: found-family spark amid desolation.

chapters.title: Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: They reach the mountain's mouth and meet the Gatekeeper, who demands a toll: a true story freely given. Juniper pays with his childhood memories of Wren. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: grief as currency, love measured in what it costs to remember.

chapters.title: The Undermarket
chapters.summary: Inside, a vast market trades in intangibles—names, regrets, unlived years. Juniper learns Wren's soul is held as collateral by Lady Vess, the Undercourt's creditor-in-chief. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror at what survival costs down here.

chapters.title: Audience with Lady Vess
chapters.summary: Vess offers Juniper a deal: walk away and live comfortably, or contest the claim and risk everything. She shows him his parents' signature—the bargain was made to save him, not Wren. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: guilt detonating; the debt was always his.

chapters.title: Maren's Secret
chapters.summary: Maren is revealed as Vess's spy—or so it seems—until she betrays Vess instead, having grown attached to Juniper. The escape plan collapses; Halvard is captured. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over origin.

chapters.title: The Archive of Sold Things
chapters.summary: Juniper infiltrates the Undercourt archive where contracts are stored as living moths in lanterns. He finds the Whitlock contract but cannot take it without a counter-payment of equal weight. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: ingenuity sharpened by desperation.

chapters.title: Brother Cassian Descends
chapters.summary: Cassian arrives with temple forces, intending to burn the Undercourt's records and Juniper with them. Chaos erupts in the market; alliances shift in the firelight. POV: Cassian. Emotional beat: zealotry meeting consequences.

chapters.title: Halvard's Bargain
chapters.summary: Imprisoned Halvard offers Vess his own remaining years in exchange for stalling the contract's completion, buying Juniper two moons. He confesses he helped draft the original wards—and the original sales. POV: Halvard. Emotional beat: atonement as a slow, expensive act.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Name
chapters.summary: Juniper learns what equal payment means: the Undercourt values identity itself. He begins drafting a counter-contract surrendering his name, lineage, and place in the world's memory. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal and personal.

chapters.title: Twelfth Moon Rising
chapters.summary: With one turn left, Juniper and Maren stage a heist to retrieve Wren's soul-lantern from Vess's vault, using smuggler knowledge of the mountain's old ore tunnels. Partial success: they get the lantern but trigger the alarm. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: Vess Unmasked
chapters.summary: Cornered, Vess reveals she was once a surface child sold like Wren, who chose power over return. She offers Juniper her old bargain one final time. He refuses. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: mirror-image villainy; pity without absolution.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: At the threshold on the final moonrise, Juniper signs the counter-contract before the assembled Undercourt, surrendering his name as Wren's soul is released upward. The mountain begins to forget him even as he speaks. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: climax—self-erasure as the ultimate act of belonging.

chapters.title: Waking Without a Name
chapters.summary: Juniper surfaces on the mountainside as stars reignite overhead, but no one remembers him—not Wren, not the temple records. Only Maren, half-underworld herself, retains a thread of him. POV: Wren, feeling an inexplicable grief. Emotional beat: bittersweet freedom; inheritance finally paid in full.

chapters.title: A New Signature
chapters.summary: Maren gives Juniper a blank ledger page and a pen: names can be written anew. Together they begin building a life outside temple and court alike, while Wren, drawn by instinct, leaves an offering at their old well. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: authorship of self; belonging chosen rather than inherited.

chapters.title: The Stars Remember
chapters.summary: Months later, the restored wards hum with a new signature no archive can trace. Wren finds a sigil carved at the well matching one on Juniper's hand, and smiles at a stranger she somehow knows. POV: Wren closing to Juniper coda. Emotional beat: resolution—love outlasting memory, the truest inheritance.
